items.title: Heavy-duty vehicle CO2-based road charges amended by EU directive
items.headline: EU directive lets member states vary road charges for heavy-duty vehicles based on CO2 emissions.
items.summary: Directive (EU) 2026/2610, adopted by the European Parliament and Council on 25 November 2026, amends Directive 1999/62/EC so that charges for heavy-duty vehicles can vary according to their CO2 emissions. It also clarifies and simplifies several other provisions of the road charging framework.
items.interest_reason: Relevant to emissions policy and carbon pricing for transport, though not a core ETS topic.

items.title: ENTSO-E proposes measures to speed up grid connections
items.headline: ENTSO-E sets out practical TSO measures to shorten grid connection times across Europe.
items.summary: The European Network of Transmission System Operators for Electricity (ENTSO-E) published its report "Accelerating Grid Connections: What TSOs Propose". Drawing on transmission operators' experience, it sets out measures to help projects connect sooner, make better use of available grid capacity and give applicants greater clarity.
items.interest_reason: Matches the reader's interest in grid expansion and connection bottlenecks.

items.title: ACER guidance on REMIT data reporting authorisation
items.headline: ACER publishes guidance for platforms seeking authorisation to report energy data under REMIT.
items.summary: The EU Agency for the Cooperation of Energy Regulators (ACER) has published new guidance for inside information platforms and registered reporting mechanisms. It helps them prepare for authorisation to report energy data to ACER under the REMIT market integrity framework.
items.interest_reason: Procedural market-oversight guidance, of limited interest to the reader's topics.

items.title: Commission implementing decision on gas cooking appliance standards
items.headline: Commission amends harmonised standards for gas cooking appliances and gas shut-off valves.
items.summary: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2026/2611, dated 26 November 2026, amends Implementing Decision (EU) 2024/2944 on harmonised standards for domestic gas cooking appliances and automatic shut-off valves for gas burners and appliances. The standards are drafted in support of EU regulation.
items.interest_reason: Technical product standards, only loosely connected to the reader's gas interests.

items.title: Delegated regulation sets carbon farming certification methods
items.headline: Commission adopts delegated regulation on certifying carbon farming activities.
items.summary: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2026/2617, dated 9 July 2026, supplements Regulation (EU) 2024/3012 by establishing certification methodologies for carbon farming activities. It was published in the Official Journal on 26 November 2026.
items.interest_reason: Carbon removal certification, peripheral to the reader's ETS and energy focus.

items.title: Council media advisory for transport and energy meeting
items.headline: Council announces agenda and press details for its 30 November to 1 December transport and telecoms session.
items.summary: The Council of the EU has issued a media advisory for the Transport, Telecommunications and Energy Council (Transport and Telecommunications) meeting on 30 November and 1 December 2026. It lists main agenda items, approximate timing, public sessions and press opportunities.
items.interest_reason: Procedural notice with no energy or ETS substance.

items.title: Europe's transport noise exposure remains high
items.headline: More than one in five Europeans face transport noise linked to sleep disruption and heart disease.
items.summary: Euractiv reports that more than one in five Europeans are exposed to transport noise at levels linked to disrupted sleep and heart disease. The item is a brief teaser without further detail on policy responses.
items.interest_reason: Noise pollution falls outside the reader's energy and ETS profile.

items.title: Vonovia installs prefabricated heat pump units in 80 apartments
items.headline: Vonovia is using prefabricated heat pump units from Enercube to speed up retrofits in apartment buildings.
items.summary: Vonovia has installed prefabricated heating centres from Enercube in 80 apartments, aiming to cut the time and cost of planning and installing heat pumps in existing multi-family buildings. The housing group plans to convert 20,000 apartments within three years using this approach.
items.interest_reason: Matches the profile's interest in residential heat pump rollout

items.title: Wood Mackenzie: EU inverter restrictions would slow solar and storage build-out to 2030
items.headline: Wood Mackenzie warns EU inverter restrictions could curb solar and storage additions through 2030.
items.summary: Analysts at Wood Mackenzie estimate that between 2027 and 2030, more than 21 GW of European demand for solar inverters and 13 GW for storage inverters would be affected by EU restrictions. Large solar and storage projects in Central and Eastern Europe are particularly at risk unless EU funding is secured.
items.interest_reason: Relevant to storage and solar policy, though focused on Central and Eastern Europe

items.title: Co-location rules: what developers must decide by end of 2026
items.headline: A lawyer explains what solar and battery operators need to decide before the planned AgNes reform takes effect.
items.summary: Lawyer Margarete von Oppen of Orka answers questions from a pv magazine webinar on the planned AgNes reform. The key issue is whether projects reaching a final investment decision in time keep legal protection under the reform, which matters for standalone large-scale storage as well as solar plants with and without batteries.
items.interest_reason: Directly covers storage and solar rules with a near-term deadline

items.title: Energy monitoring report: renewables reach 55 percent, but power cut-offs rise
items.headline: Germany's competition watchdog and regulator report renewables at 55 percent but more electricity disconnections.
items.summary: The Federal Cartel Office and the Bundesnetzagentur have published their energy monitoring report. It finds renewables reaching a 55 percent share, while the number of electricity disconnections has increased, set against ongoing price shocks in power and gas.
items.interest_reason: Covers grid outages and disconnections, a core profile topic

items.title: Greens demand crisis package against rising heating costs
items.headline: The Greens call on the government for targeted relief as heating costs threaten households this winter.
items.summary: Green parliamentary leader Dröge warns that families face a sharp rise in heating costs this winter. Her party is calling on the federal government to introduce targeted relief measures against increasing energy costs.
items.interest_reason: Energy prices are relevant, but this is political rather than technical

items.title: Refinery margins shrink as fuel prices fall faster than crude
items.headline: Fuel prices are falling faster than crude oil, easing inflation pressure, though still far above pre-war levels.
items.summary: Refinery margins in Germany have shrunk significantly despite the Iran war, Handelsblatt reports. Fuel prices are dropping faster than crude oil prices, which reduces near-term inflation pressure for consumers, companies and central banks, but levels remain well above those before the conflict.
items.interest_reason: Refining economics fit the profile's hydrogen and refinery interests only loosely

items.title: Scientists back more solar and storage build-out in appeal
items.headline: Sixty scientists have signed an appeal backing faster solar and battery storage expansion in Germany.
items.summary: Sixty researchers, the first signatories of an appeal launched by the Bundesverband Solar- & Batteriewirtschaft (BSB, the German solar and battery industry association), call for more investment certainty for PV and better use of storage flexibility. They also urge faster storage build-out and digitalisation.
items.interest_reason: Relevant to storage and flexibility, but an advocacy appeal rather than a policy decision

items.title: Environment ministers adopt guidelines on water scarcity
items.headline: Germany's environment ministers have adopted guidelines for managing water scarcity at their conference in Bad Schandau.
items.summary: The Environment Ministers' Conference adopted guidelines on handling water scarcity in Bad Schandau. The decision implements a key measure of the National Water Strategy.
items.interest_reason: Environmental policy, but outside the profile's energy focus

items.title: Bundesnetzagentur issues HEDWIG rules on energy market data
items.headline: The Bundesnetzagentur has issued HEDWIG, a determination governing collection and publication of energy market data.
items.summary: The Bundesnetzagentur has issued a determination called HEDWIG that sets out how energy market data is collected and published. The source provides no further details.
items.interest_reason: Market data rules are relevant to market transparency, though details are limited

items.title: Economists' call for cheap power met with a rebuttal on solar and biogas
items.headline: A FAZ commentary argues that the energy transition is more than a cost calculation, answering 26 economists.
items.summary: A FAZ commentary responds to a call by 26 economists for the cheapest possible power supply. The author argues that the energy transition cannot be judged on cost alone, with photovoltaics and biogas as examples.
items.interest_reason: Opinion piece on a general debate, with little new substance

items.title: Petroleum federation says Belgian refineries help cushion the energy crisis
items.headline: Belgium's two large Antwerp refineries are helping supply the country during the current energy crisis.
items.summary: The Petroleum Federation Energia argues that the two large refineries in the Antwerp port make a major contribution to Belgium's energy supply during the current energy crisis. Keeping that role, however, requires heavy investment, with 20 billion euros needed to make the plants low-CO2 by 2050.
items.interest_reason: Refineries and fossil fuel transition fit the profile closely.

items.title: Elia raises 2026 earnings forecast despite US write-down
items.headline: Grid operator Elia has raised its full-year forecast thanks to higher interest rates, despite a US setback.
items.summary: Belgian grid operator Elia has raised its expectations for the full year, as rising interest rates benefit its regulated assets. The update comes despite a new write-down of its US activity, where higher rates work against the company.
items.interest_reason: Grid operator finances relate to grid expansion and tariffs in profile.
